newsitem.title: GERMANY: EU not to budge on VW subsidy row - paper.
newsitem.headline: EU not to budge on VW subsidy row - paper.

text.p: The European Commission is to continue to demand repayment of all state subsidies paid to German carmaker Volkswagen that contravene a Commission ruling on the matter, a newspaper said on Sunday.
German business daily Handelsblatt quoted European Commission competition official Alexander Schaub as saying that the EC would demand repayment all grants blocked by it in a June 1996 ruling.
Until VW paid back those funds, the EC would block any further subsidies for VW projects, the newspaper said in the summary of an article to appear on Monday.
Volkswagen was not immediately available to comment.

in June last year the Commission cleared almost 540 million marks of regional subsidies to VW's Mosel and Chemnitz plants in the German state of Saxony. That was some 241 million marks less than orginally promised by the Saxony government.
The German government has sought to defuse the conflict by blocking tax rebates to the firm in a move to neutralise the disputed aid.
